summary.text: A female infant born by cesarean section at 32+2 weeks to a mother with COVID-19 respiratory failure required CPAP at delivery and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory distress and prematurity; ABO incompatibility was present and she received 12 h of phototherapy.

Bilirubin rose over the first days (direct 0.9 mg/dL at 12 h and 1.3 mg/dL on DOL 3) with GGT 1044 U/L on DOL 4; ultrasound suggested a Type 1 choledochal cyst, while MRCP with Eovist on DOL 6 showed a 1.2 cm porta hepatis cyst, an abnormal slit-like gallbladder and no Eovist excretion, more concerning for cystic biliary atresia, and a confirmatory cholangiogram was recommended.

Ursodiol and fat-soluble vitamins were started; liver biopsy on DOL 23 was concerning for early biliary atresia and the intraoperative cholangiogram on DOL 46 confirmed Type III cystic biliary atresia, followed by Kasai hepatoportoenterostomy with excision of the cystic biliary atresia and Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy.

The postoperative course was uneventful with discharge home on DOL 55; she is now 2 years old, followed by transplant hepatology, growing appropriately with normal native liver synthetic function and without clinically significant portal hypertension.

summary.text: A 17-day-old infant (born at 39+2 weeks after induced vaginal delivery for polyhydramnios; prenatal scan at 13 weeks concerning for pancreatic and choroid plexus cysts, the latter resolving) presented with direct hyperbilirubinemia after postnatal phototherapy, with initial clay colored stool and pigmented stool at presentation.

On DOL 10 total and direct bilirubin were 18.4 and 2.4 mg/dL with GGT 1251 U/L; ursodiol and vitamins were started, ultrasound suggested a Type 1 choledochal cyst, and MRCP with Eovist on DOL 17 showed a 2.3 cm porta hepatis cyst, a small caliber gallbladder and no Eovist excretion, concerning for cystic biliary atresia with choledochal cyst not fully excluded.

Intraoperative cholangiogram on DOL 20 confirmed Type III cystic biliary atresia, followed by Kasai hepatoportoenterostomy with excision and Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy; biopsy showed cholestatic hepatitis consistent with BA, the postoperative course was uneventful and she was discharged on DOL 26.

Direct bilirubin normalized at 4 months, but the post-KHPE course was complicated by compensated advanced chronic liver disease and portal hypertension with caput medusae; liver biopsy at 6 months was consistent with cirrhosis and she underwent living-related donor liver transplant at 11 months, with post-transplant EBV/CMV viremia, thrombocytopenia, portal vein stenosis and gastrointestinal bleeding; at 2 years old she is growing appropriately with normal synthetic function and mild hemodynamically insignificant portal vein stenosis.
